questions.q: Project 18A, approved by the Defence Acquisition Council, is a programme for:
questions.explanation: A **₹80,000-crore destroyer** programme with ~75% indigenous content.
questions.fact_text: The Defence Acquisition Council gave in-principle approval to a **₹80,000-crore** next-generation guided-missile destroyer programme (Project 18A) with nearly 75% indigenous content, to be designed by the Navy's Warship Design Bureau, amid growing Chinese and Pakistani underwater-warfare capabilities.

questions.q: Gross GST collection in October 2026 was:
questions.explanation: **₹2.31 lakh crore**, up 23%.
questions.fact_text: GST collections rose **23% y-o-y in October to ₹2.31 lakh crore** — the second-highest monthly figure ever and the fastest growth this fiscal year; October was the second straight month gross GST crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and April-October gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore.

questions.q: The 2027-28 Union Budget allocated how much to the Department of Space?
questions.explanation: **₹17,000 crore**, up from ₹13,705.6 crore.
questions.fact_text: Following the successful GSLV-F18 launch of the NVS-03 satellite, the 2027-28 Union Budget allocated **₹17,000 crore** to the Department of Space (up from ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27), after two PSLV failures over the preceding 18 months.

also.text: ISRO chairman **V. Narayanan**: NVS-03 flew with **three pyro valves open** (to avoid NVS-02's orbit-raising failure), cleared by a committee under ex-chief **A.S. Kiran Kumar**. **NavIC** is back to its minimum of **four** satellites; **NVS-04** is due in 5 months and **NVS-05** in 10. Orbit: perigee 170.31 km (planned 170.36).

questions.q: India's installed solar capacity has grown from 2.8 GW in 2014 to about:
questions.explanation: About **171 GW**; target 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030.
questions.fact_text: India's installed solar capacity grew from **2.8 GW (2014) to 171 GW**, with solar tariffs falling from about ₹8/unit to as low as ₹2.15/unit; under PM Surya Ghar, 21+ lakh of a 65-lakh-home target now have zero electricity bills; the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit (Bharat Mandapam, 2-5 Nov) hosts the 9th ISA Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen, with India targeting $220 billion in investment for 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.

also.text: **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana** was launched in **February 2024** to give up to **300 units** of free electricity a month to **1 crore** households.

questions.q: Bhutan dedicated Chorten No. 76 of its 108 stupas to:
questions.explanation: To **PM Narendra Modi**, as part of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.
questions.fact_text: Bhutan dedicated Chorten No. 76 of its **108 Buddhist stupas** (Jangchub Chortens), built in a nine-hour effort by 40,000+ volunteers, to PM Narendra Modi, as part of the India-backed Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC) project.

also.text: Bhutan's **Project 108** (announced by King **Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuk** on 26 Feb): **108 jangchub chortens**, each **15 m** tall, **108 m** apart along **12 km** of the **Mau Chhu** river in **Gelephu**, built on **1 Nov** (Buddha's Descending Day, Mother's Day, the King's **18th coronation anniversary**). Most relics are of Indian origin; each costs about **$200,000**.

questions.q: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on:
questions.explanation: **31 October**, Sardar Patel's birth anniversary (151st in 2026).
questions.fact_text: **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's** 151st birth anniversary fell on 31 October 2026 (National Unity Day/Rashtriya Ekta Diwas); retrospectives recalled his role integrating ~500 princely states and his post-Gandhi-assassination ban on the RSS, lifted after the RSS agreed to respect the tricolour.

also.text: **National Unity Day** (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, since **2014**) is on **31 Oct**, Sardar Patel's birth anniversary. Statue of Unity: **182 m**, inaugurated 2018.

questions.q: The motto adopted by the new IAF chief Ashutosh Dixit is:
questions.explanation: **Nabha Sparsham Deeptam** (also the IAF's motto), with the 'VAYU' framework.
questions.fact_text: New IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal **Ashutosh Dixit** outlined the '**VAYU**' framework — Vigilance & readiness, Aatmanirbharta, Yukti (ingenuity) and Unity of effort — and adopted the motto '*Nabha Sparsham Deeptam*', prioritising the indigenous Tejas Mk1A/Mk2 and the AMCA.

also.text: Air Chief Marshal **Ashutosh Dixit** took over as the **29th Chief of the Air Staff** on 31 October 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, who retired after 43 years of service.

questions.q: Whom did Ashutosh Dixit succeed as Chief of the Air Staff?
questions.explanation: **A.P. Singh**, who retired after 43 years.
questions.fact_text: Air Chief Marshal **Ashutosh Dixit** took over as the **29th Chief of the Air Staff** on 31 October 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, who retired after 43 years of service.

also.text: New IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal **Ashutosh Dixit** outlined the '**VAYU**' framework — Vigilance & readiness, Aatmanirbharta, Yukti (ingenuity) and Unity of effort — and adopted the motto '*Nabha Sparsham Deeptam*', prioritising the indigenous Tejas Mk1A/Mk2 and the AMCA.

questions.q: Which city did Amit Shah say will be India's first drug-free city?
questions.explanation: **Chandigarh**, with a 93% conviction rate in NDPS cases.
questions.fact_text: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said Chandigarh will be India's first city to become drug-free; Chandigarh Police have achieved a **93% conviction rate** in NDPS Act cases since the new criminal laws took effect (8,206 FIRs registered since 4 August 2024).

questions.q: EPFO celebrated which Foundation Day in 2026?
questions.explanation: The **74th**; corpus over ₹32 lakh crore.
questions.fact_text: EPFO celebrated its 74th Foundation Day; its corpus has grown to over **₹32 lakh crore**, accumulated from more than eight crore members, Union Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya said.

questions.q: Who won the 97th MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup hockey title?
questions.explanation: **Indian Navy**, beating BPCL 5-4 in a shootout.
questions.fact_text: Indian Navy beat Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) 5-4 in a penalty shootout to win the **97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup** hockey title in Chennai.

questions.q: P.V. Sindhu and Lakshya Sen won singles titles at the Hylo Open Super 500, held in:
questions.explanation: **Saarbrücken, Germany**.
questions.fact_text: **P.V. Sindhu** and **Lakshya Sen** won the women's and men's singles titles at the Hylo Open Super 500 (Saarbrucken, Germany) with straight-games final wins — Sindhu's title adds to her earlier Japan Open win this year, and Lakshya ended a title drought.

also.text: **Lakshya Sen** beat Indonesia's **Jonatan Christie** 21-17, 21-10 in the Hylo Open final, his first title of 2026 and second Hylo Open.

questions.q: Who became the highest run-scorer in a bilateral T20I series (341 runs vs India)?
questions.explanation: **Glenn Phillips**, passing Phil Salt's 331.
questions.fact_text: New Zealand's **Glenn Phillips** became the highest run-scorer in a bilateral T20I series with 341 runs against India in five matches, surpassing England's Phil Salt's 331 (2023).

also.text: New Zealand won the fifth T20I by seven wickets (Tim Seifert 93*), but **India won the series 3-2** after taking the first three games — captain **Shreyas Iyer's** first series win in a **SENA** country.

questions.q: India won the 2026 T20I series in New Zealand by what margin?
questions.explanation: **3-2**; captain Shreyas Iyer's first series win in a SENA country.
questions.fact_text: New Zealand won the fifth T20I by seven wickets (Tim Seifert 93*), but **India won the series 3-2** after taking the first three games — captain **Shreyas Iyer's** first series win in a **SENA** country.

also.text: New Zealand's **Glenn Phillips** became the highest run-scorer in a bilateral T20I series with 341 runs against India in five matches, surpassing England's Phil Salt's 331 (2023).

questions.q: The inaugural Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship was held in:
questions.explanation: **Ahmedabad**; India won both the men's and women's titles.
questions.fact_text: India's men's and women's kabaddi teams won the titles at the inaugural **Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship** in Ahmedabad; the men beat Sri Lanka 54-20 and the women beat Uganda 35-15.

questions.q: According to PLFS, India's unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to what in 2023-24?
questions.explanation: **3.2%**, though the Decent Work Index rose only from 0.247 to 0.302.
questions.fact_text: PLFS data show India's unemployment rate fell from **6.1% (2017-18) to 3.2% (2023-24)**, but a Decent Work Index (DWI) rose only from 0.247 to 0.302 over the same period; nearly 90% of the workforce remains informally employed (India Employment Report 2024, ILO-IHD), and agriculture's DWI (0.211→0.267) stayed the lowest despite four Labour Codes notified in 2025.

questions.q: The UNGA has passed a resolution against the US embargo on Cuba every year since:
questions.explanation: Since **1992**. India voted in favour again.
questions.fact_text: The UNGA's annual resolution (held every year since 1992) calling on the US to end its Cuba embargo passed on 30 October with only **130 in favour, 18 abstaining and 17 against** — sharply down from 165 in favour the year before — amid US pressure on Latin American states; India again voted in favour, calling for 'dialogue and diplomacy'.

questions.q: The RBI's inflation-targeting band for CPI inflation is:
questions.fact_text: India's headline CPI inflation, which hit multi-year lows in 2025, edged back up to **5.54% by September 2026** — still within the RBI's 2-6% inflation-targeting band, though a reminder that real returns on bank deposits stay thin.

questions.q: The long-period average (LPA) of India's southwest monsoon rainfall is about:
questions.explanation: About **87 cm**; 2026 ended nearly 13% below it.
questions.fact_text: India's 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly **13% below the long-term average** (87 cm) — the driest season on record (since 1901) for East and Northeast India — despite IMD's April forecast of 92% of the Long Period Average; of seven Indian monsoons since 1950 that coincided with a moderate/strong El Nino, five (including 2026) saw rainfall at least 10% below average, while 1997 was a rare exception because a favourable Indian Ocean Dipole phase offset El Nino's effect; the monsoon supplies about three-quarters of India's annual rainfall and roughly 40% of farmland remains unirrigated.

questions.q: The Lyngdoh Committee (2006) is associated with rules for:
questions.explanation: **Student union elections** in colleges and universities.
questions.fact_text: About 4,000 women students at Aligarh Muslim University's Women's College were denied voting rights in the AMU Students' Union elections (scheduled 5 Nov, the first in 8 years), reviving a gender-representation debate that traces back to a 2012 committee formed under the Lyngdoh Committee framework.

questions.q: Where did the INDIA bloc hold its rally against the SIR?
questions.explanation: **Ramlila Maidan**, Delhi; the BJP held a counter-rally on the 1984 riots.
questions.fact_text: Rahul Gandhi accused Chief Election Commissioner **Gyanesh Kumar** of 'treason' over the SIR, calling it 'theft of every citizen's voice'; the INDIA bloc held a rally at **Ramlila Maidan**, Delhi, with the Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav calling it the 'Haldighati of democracy'.

questions.q: Over 1,000 discrepant entries after the SIR were found in which city's rolls?
questions.explanation: **Bengaluru**, including the Dasarahalli constituency.
questions.fact_text: *The Hindu* found over 1,000 discrepant entries (garbled names, missing relatives' names) in Bengaluru's final electoral rolls published after the Special Intensive Revision, e.g. in the Dasarahalli Assembly constituency (part 324).

questions.q: Under which Schedule did the RJD seek the disqualification of two Bihar MLCs?
questions.explanation: The **Tenth Schedule** (anti-defection).
questions.fact_text: Bihar: Independent MLCs **Bansidhar Brajwasi** (Tirhut Graduates' seat) and **Rahul Raj** (Saran Teachers' seat) were announced as having 'joined' the BJP, then described an hour later as only having 'extended support'; RJD's Tejashwi Yadav sought their disqualification under the **Tenth Schedule**.

questions.q: West Bengal aims to give CAA citizenship to 2.5 lakh people of which community?
questions.explanation: **Matuas**, Hindu Namasudras with roots in Bangladesh.
questions.fact_text: West Bengal's government said it aims to grant citizenship under the **CAA** to **2.5 lakh Matuas** (Hindu Namasudras with roots in Bangladesh) by 31 December 2026; only 25,000 have received citizenship under the CAA so far.

questions.q: Turnout in Andhra Pradesh's 2026 urban local body polls was:
questions.fact_text: Andhra Pradesh held civic polls for 13 municipal corporations and 79 municipalities/nagar panchayats; overall turnout was **48.03%** (vs 63.30% in 2021), with Machilipatnam highest (55.10%) and Greater Visakhapatnam lowest (39.72%); YSRCP's Jagan Mohan Reddy demanded a repoll in Pulivendula alleging malpractice.

questions.q: How many cases are pending in India's High Courts, per the CJI?
questions.explanation: **65,54,788**, with 292 judicial vacancies against a sanctioned 1,122.
questions.fact_text: CJI **Surya Kant** flagged litigants' 'growing tendency' to rush to the Supreme Court for early hearings even as **65,54,788 cases** remain pending in High Courts (25 High Courts face 292 judicial vacancies against a sanctioned strength of 1,122) and the Supreme Court's own backlog nears one lakh (97,201 cases).

questions.q: India's power consumption in October 2026 grew by:
questions.explanation: **21.88%** year-on-year, to 159.76 billion units.
questions.fact_text: India's power consumption grew **21.88% y-o-y in October to 159.76 billion units**, while Coal India Ltd's production rose 19.3% y-o-y to 67.2 million tonnes.

questions.q: A 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder in Delhi cost how much after the November revision?
questions.explanation: **₹2,820**; Kolkata's rose to ₹2,971. Domestic LPG was unchanged.
questions.fact_text: Commercial LPG prices rose for a third straight time (Delhi 19-kg cylinder up ₹10 to ₹2,820; Kolkata saw the steepest hike of ₹17 to ₹2,971) and ATF (jet fuel) rose ₹1.37/litre to ₹138.5 — the fourth hike since July — while domestic LPG prices were left unchanged.

questions.q: Foreign Portfolio Investors withdrew how much from Indian equities in October?
questions.explanation: **₹34,843 crore**, a second straight month of outflows.
questions.fact_text: Foreign Portfolio Investors withdrew **₹34,843 crore** from Indian equities in October (second straight month of heavy outflows), per Central Depository Services data, amid concerns over crude oil prices and global interest rates.

questions.q: Comex gold fell in October 2026 to a one-year low of about:
questions.explanation: **$3,884.9 an ounce**, down 7.26%; silver fell 19.1%.
questions.fact_text: Comex gold fell 7.26% in October to a one-year low of $3,884.9/ounce, while Comex silver dropped 19.1% to $49.13/ounce, as both precious metals posted negative returns for a second straight month.

questions.q: On day one of Delhi's entry curbs, how many vehicles were turned back?
questions.explanation: **714** of 7,279 checked; 38 end-of-life vehicles were impounded.
questions.fact_text: Delhi's winter entry curbs on non-BS-VI, non-Delhi-registered vehicles began Sunday and run till 31 January; on Day 1, police checked 7,279 vehicles, turned back 714 non-destined vehicles and impounded 38 end-of-life vehicles.

questions.q: Cyclone Arnab's losses in Andhra Pradesh were estimated at:
questions.explanation: **₹4,600 crore**, with 3.5 lakh hectares of crops submerged.
questions.fact_text: **Cyclone Murasu** was expected to make landfall on Tuesday between Nellore and Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh) with gusts up to 120 km/h, days after **Cyclone Arnab** killed five, submerged 3.5 lakh hectares of crops, damaged 2,425 km of roads and ~15,000 electric poles, and caused an estimated ₹4,600 crore in losses; AP put five districts (SPSR Nellore, Prakasam, Guntur, Bapatla, Krishna) on red alert and mobilised 1,688 medical teams and 116 relief camps.

questions.q: Delhi's planned 3.3-km heritage corridor runs along:
questions.explanation: **Netaji Subhash Marg**, from Delhi Gate to Kashmere Gate.
questions.fact_text: Delhi CM **Rekha Gupta** announced a 3.3-km heritage corridor along Netaji Subhash Marg from Delhi Gate to Kashmere Gate, covering the Red Fort, St James' Church and Chandni Chowk, with a Heritage Interpretation Park planned at Delhi Gate.

questions.q: China's CPC Fifth Plenum confirmed the expulsion of how many Central Committee members?
questions.explanation: **33**, including 16 PLA generals.
questions.fact_text: China's CPC **Fifth Plenum** (concluded 29 Oct) confirmed the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members, including 16 PLA Generals (e.g. Miao Hua, Zhang Youxia); only 279 of 376 full Central Committee members (elected 2022) remained present, ahead of the 21st Party Congress expected in late 2027, when Xi Jinping could seek an unprecedented fourth term.

questions.q: What did Iran's Revolutionary Guards say a renewed war would have?
questions.explanation: '**No geographic limitations**', Iran warned.
questions.fact_text: Iran warned that any renewed war with the US 'could last longer' than the previous round, after President Trump said he had to 'take care of' more targets; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a future conflict would have 'no geographic limitations'.

questions.q: Lula beat Flavio Bolsonaro in the runoff by what margin?
questions.fact_text: Brazil's **Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva** won a **fourth** presidential term, beating Jair Bolsonaro-backed Flavio Bolsonaro **51.79% to 48.21%** in the runoff after trailing in the first round; Lula has backed the New Development Bank and BRICS local-currency trade, while Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro was reportedly taken to the US for trial in January 2026.

questions.q: Pakistan told which government that 'terrorism is a red line'?
questions.explanation: Afghanistan's **Taliban** government.
questions.fact_text: Pakistan warned Afghanistan's Taliban government that 'terrorism is a red line' and that Pakistan's national security 'cannot be held hostage to the Taliban regime's inaction', amid deteriorating bilateral ties.

questions.q: Harvard's ElectIt model forecast Democrats winning how many of 435 House seats?
questions.explanation: **230**, plus 18 of the 35 contested Senate seats.
questions.fact_text: Harvard's ElectIt model (Gary King et al.) forecast Democrats winning **230 of 435 House seats** and 18 of 35 contested Senate seats in the US midterms; President Trump's approval stood near 37% against ~60% disapproval, and the generic ballot showed Democrats leading 51%-42%.

questions.q: Mahadev Online Book promoter Sourabh Chandrakar was extradited from:
questions.explanation: **Oman**, after an Interpol Red Corner Notice.
questions.fact_text: **Sourabh Chandrakar**, promoter of the Mahadev Online Book illegal betting app (scam pegged at ₹6,000 crore, run via franchised 'panels' and 'branches'), was extradited to India from Oman following an Interpol Red Corner Notice, in a CBI-led operation.

questions.q: Azam Khan's PMLA case relates to land taken for which institution?
questions.explanation: **Mohammad Ali Jauhar University**, Rampur.
questions.fact_text: Samajwadi Party leader **Azam Khan** was sent to 14-day judicial custody by a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad in an ED money-laundering case based on 26 FIRs (2019) alleging forced occupation of farmers' land in Rampur for Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.

questions.q: Which group did Chainalysis blame for the $6.3-billion Binance hack?
questions.explanation: North Korea's **Lazarus Group**, via 'TraderTraitor'.
questions.fact_text: **Binance**, the world's largest crypto exchange, suffered a cyberattack on 29 October with losses estimated at over **$6.3 billion**; analytics firm Chainalysis attributed it to North Korea's Lazarus Group (via 'TraderTraitor'), similar to the 2024 WazirX hack ($235 million); stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze 1.567bn USDT and 800m USDC respectively.

questions.q: The alleged rape inside a police station that led to three arrests was in:
questions.explanation: **Seraikela, Jharkhand**; an SIT was formed.
questions.fact_text: A Sub-Inspector and a constable were arrested (taking the total to three arrests) over an alleged rape inside a police station in **Seraikela, Jharkhand**; a Special Investigation Team was formed under SP Manoj Swargiary.

questions.q: Which university ordered a probe into a first-year student's molestation complaint?
questions.explanation: **Jadavpur University**, Kolkata.
questions.fact_text: Jadavpur University ordered a probe after a first-year Arts student alleged molestation by a non-teaching staffer on campus; Vice-Chancellor Chiranjib Bhattacharjee ordered the inquiry.

questions.q: West Bengal offered Group D jobs to families of those killed in political violence over the past:
questions.explanation: **25 years**, with an income cutoff of ₹50,000 a month.
questions.fact_text: West Bengal's government notified Group D government jobs for one family member of each person killed in political violence over the preceding 25 years (income cutoff ₹50,000/month), a day after CM Suvendu Adhikari's announcement in Paschim Medinipur.

questions.q: Carlos Alcaraz won which title by beating Alex de Minaur?
options: Erste Bank Open final in Madrid
questions.explanation: The **Vienna Open**, his fourth title of 2026.
questions.fact_text: **Carlos Alcaraz** beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open — his fourth title of the year and 28th overall.

questions.q: Marc Marquez closed on which milestone after winning the Malaysian GP?
questions.explanation: An **eighth MotoGP world title**; his lead grew to 399 points.
questions.fact_text: **Marc Marquez** moved to the brink of an eighth MotoGP world title after winning the Malaysian GP, extending his points lead to 399 (second-placed brother Alex Marquez on 355) with three race weekends left.

questions.q: Manav Thakkar won his first international singles title at:
questions.explanation: **WTT Feeder Chennai**, beating England's Samuel Walker.
questions.fact_text: **Manav Thakkar** won his first international singles title at **WTT Feeder Chennai**, beating England's Samuel Walker in the final; **Sutirtha Mukherjee** was runner-up in women's singles to Korea's Yoo Yerin.
